title: Anthony of Padua (13 June)
hookLine: a great Franciscan preacher, now asked to find lost things

lines: A VOICE THAT FILLED A SQUARE.
cards: A passport the night before a flight. Somewhere, right now, someone is turning a couch cushion over again and saying, half joking and half not, Saint Anthony, help.
Day one thousand on this path, and its saint is one whose name gets said in kitchens and parking lots. But he started as a voice that filled a square. Today, Anthony of Padua.

teach.h: FROM LISBON TO AN UNKNOWN FRIAR.
teach.b: Anthony was born in Lisbon, in Portugal, and became a canon, then a Franciscan friar, drawn to the order of Francis of Assisi while Francis was still alive. He hoped to go to Morocco as a missionary.

Illness sent him back, a storm blew his ship off course, and he ended up in Italy, an unknown friar. Then one day, the story goes, at an ordination no one was ready to preach, and Anthony was told to say something.
He opened his mouth, and the room discovered he knew the Scriptures deeply. From then on he preached across Italy and France, to crowds that filled churches and spilled into squares.
The Church later named him a Doctor of the Church.
So how does a great preacher become the saint of lost keys?
Tradition says a young friar who was leaving the order took Anthony's book of psalms with him, a book Anthony had filled with notes for his preaching. Anthony prayed for it.
The young man returned the book, and came back to the community too. Something precious lost and found, and a person along with it. That's an old pattern in the Gospels.

Jesus tells of a woman who sweeps her whole house for one silver coin, and when she finds it she calls in the neighbors. In the Douay-Rheims: "Rejoice with me, because I have found the groat which I had lost."
In Catholic teaching, asking Anthony's help isn't a lucky charm.

teach.h: A FRIEND ASKED TO PRAY WITH YOU.
teach.b: It's asking a friend in heaven to pray with you, as you'd ask a friend at the table.

teach.h: I HAVE FOUND THE GROAT WHICH I HAD LOST.
teach.b: And some pray to him for things bigger than keys: a lost faith, a lost child, a friendship gone quiet.

how: The Church keeps the memorial of Saint Anthony of Padua on 13 June; Catholics ask his intercession when something is lost, and some parishes bless and hand out bread on his feast, called Saint Anthony's bread, for the poor.

o: the Italian city linked to Saint Anthony

games.q: Anthony of Padua — tap the pairs.
p: where he hoped to go as a missionary
taken by a young friar, then returned

s: he was born in Lisbon, in Portugal; Padua is where he's remembered by name.
he was first known as a well-known preacher
he arrived in Italy unknown; the story says he was asked to preach without warning.
the lost-things story involves a book of psalms
tradition says a departing friar took Anthony's annotated psalter and brought it back.

games.q: you're a young friar leaving the order. you've taken Anthony's book of psalms, full of his notes. what does the story say happens?
o: you sell it and never look back.
you return the book, and come back yourself.
Anthony writes a new one and forgets it.
games.why: tradition says the young man brought the book back and returned to the community: both were found.

practice: Let one lost thing come to mind, small and annoying, or not a thing at all: a habit of prayer, a person you've drifted from.

Name it plainly, once, and don't search yet; just hold it, the way the woman lit her candle before she swept. If you pray, ask Saint Anthony to pray with you for it; if you don't, simply admit you'd like it back.

wordCard.voice: Padua, the Italian city linked to the Franciscan preacher Anthony, born in Lisbon, now asked by Catholics to help them find what's lost.

orig.note: Greek: 'I found' — the woman's cry over her lost coin in Luke 15:9.

carryVoice: Your line: finder of lost things. In his story, a book came home, and a person came with it. One thousand days now.
